headline: Medium prompt-injection and data-leakage risks arise from shared document/LLM workflows; no direct evidence of a blocking control between Cognee and MinerU.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cognee ingests documents and session memory, while MinerU parses PDFs/DOCX/XLSX and exposes an MCP server. If MinerU outputs are fed into Cognee without provenance filtering, attacker-controlled document text can become instructions. The pairwise pathway is plausible in default document workflows, though not directly documented.
conditions: IF MinerU outputs are forwarded into Cognee as trusted text or prompts
IF an MCP bridge passes document content without provenance tags
mitigations: Add a provenance prefix to all MinerU outputs before Cognee ingests them
Disable automatic prompt-following on extracted text
Route only quoted snippets, not raw documents, into Cognee
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction-stripping at the integration boundary

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cognee touches personal data, finance data, support history, and documents; MinerU reads local office/PDF files and can expose them through API/MCP workflows. Even though MinerU is described as fully offline, the pair can still leak sensitive file contents if shared inputs or logs are reused across the boundary.
conditions: IF the same sensitive files are processed by MinerU and then stored in Cognee session memory
IF API or MCP logs retain extracted text from protected documents
mitigations: Restrict the integration to non-sensitive documents only
Turn off or minimize logging on the MinerU API/MCP layer
Separate storage locations for raw files and Cognee memory
requires-engineering: implement field-level redaction before persistence

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Cognee supports multiple instances and session memory; MinerU supports multi-threaded concurrent inference and an MCP server. That creates a plausible write/coordination conflict around shared outputs or shared mutable resources, even though MinerU itself cannot write files and Cognee's filesystem write surface is not listed.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable workspace or database
IF the MCP server exposes shared state without locking
mitigations: Assign separate workspaces per agent
Serialize writes through a single orchestrator
Disable concurrent runs against the same dataset
requires-engineering: add locking or optimistic concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: MinerU produces extracted text, tables, OCR, and formulas; Cognee stores decisions, workflows, and successful implementations. If Cognee treats MinerU output as authoritative, extraction errors can cascade into incorrect downstream memory or decisions. The pairwise risk is plausible because both profiles show document-processing-to-memory flow, but verification is absent.
conditions: IF Cognee ingests MinerU extraction results without validation
IF downstream workflows act on extracted tables or OCR as ground truth
mitigations: Require human review for extracted facts before storage
Compare MinerU output against source documents for critical fields
Mark extracted content as untrusted metadata
requires-engineering: add validation rules for high-impact fields

E_compliance.rationale: Cognee explicitly touches personal data and finance data, while MinerU processes local documents and offers API/MCP surfaces. If regulated documents are routed through MinerU into Cognee, retention or residency obligations can diverge. The profiles do not show a direct certification mismatch, so this is a compliance-gap risk rather than a breach certainty.
conditions: IF regulated personal or finance documents are processed through both agents
IF retention or deletion policies differ between MinerU logs and Cognee memory
mitigations: Use only de-identified documents in the pair
Set a short retention window for extracted text
Document a deletion workflow for both systems
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls across the integration
